Tables by trial and treatment arm

Source: vignettes/articles/multi-trial-tables.Rmd
multi-trial-tables.Rmd
library(niceSMD)

When you pool individual participant data from several trials (for example in a trial-level surrogate endpoint analysis), nice_trial_table1() summarizes each trial separately, by treatment arm. Under the hood each trial is run through nice_SMD_table1(), so every convention (denominators, missing values, weights, SMDs) is identical; the function arranges the pieces into one table.

Example data

example_trial_data() has three trials. Trials A and B compare Placebo with Active; Trial C adds a High dose arm.

d <- example_trial_data()
table(d$trial, d$arm)
#>          
#>           Placebo Active High dose
#>   Trial A      30     30         0
#>   Trial B      24     24         0
#>   Trial C      24     24        24

Trials side by side 

vars <- c("age", "egfr", "sex", "diabetes", "ckd_stage")
labels <- c("Age (years)", "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2)", "Sex", "Diabetes", "CKD stage")

wide <- nice_trial_table1(
  d, trial = "trial", treatment = "arm", covar_names = vars,
  print_covariate_names = labels,
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),   # required: Trial C has 3 arms
  notes = "short"
)

Summaries are computed within each trial and treatment arm. Categorical: n (%) among nonmissing values. Continuous: mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3). Missing: n (% of arm).

SMD = absolute standardized mean difference (Placebo vs. Active); NE = not estimable.

A Missing row is shown only for variables with at least one missing value in some trial.

Things to notice:

  • A header spans each trial; arms sit underneath with their sample sizes.
  • The SMD in each trial compares only the two arms named in treatment_for_SMD. Trial C’s High dose arm is shown but not compared.
  • ckd_stage G5 does not occur in Trial A, so it displays as a zero count.
  • A Missing row appears only for age and eGFR, the only variables with missing values (show_missing = "if_any" is the default here).

This layout works for a few trials. With many trials it becomes too wide.

One row per trial and arm 

long <- nice_trial_table1(
  d, "trial", "arm", vars, print_covariate_names = labels,
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
  layout = "long", continuous_stats = "mean_sd", notes = "short"
)

Summaries are computed within each trial and treatment arm. Categorical: n (%) among nonmissing values. Continuous: mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3). Missing: n (% of arm).

A Missing row is shown only for variables with at least one missing value in some trial.

Variables run across the columns, categorical variables get one column per level, and each trial’s rows are grouped. continuous_stats = "mean_sd" keeps only mean (SD), which roughly halves the width. SMDs are not shown in this layout, but they are always available:

head(long$smd[, c("trial", "label", "smd", "status")], 6)
#>     trial                 label         smd status
#> 1 Trial A           Age (years) 0.154448370     ok
#> 2 Trial A eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) 0.001980403     ok
#> 3 Trial A                   Sex 0.000000000     ok
#> 4 Trial A              Diabetes 0.134839972     ok
#> 5 Trial A             CKD stage 0.000000000     ok
#> 6 Trial B           Age (years) 0.355183343     ok

Should the table include SMDs at all?

Within a randomized trial, baseline differences between arms are chance imbalances, and reporting guidance discourages baseline significance tests. Many authors therefore omit within-trial SMDs. To drop the SMD columns from the wide table:

nice_trial_table1(d, "trial", "arm", vars, treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
                  show_smd = FALSE)

Weights, order, and export 

# Weighted summaries within each trial and arm
nice_trial_table1(d, "trial", "arm", vars, weights = "weight",
                  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"))

# Put trials and arms in a chosen order
nice_trial_table1(d, "trial", "arm", vars,
                  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
                  trial_order = c("Trial C", "Trial A", "Trial B"),
                  treatment_order = c("Active", "Placebo", "High dose"))

# Word (landscape is recommended for trial tables)
save_table1_docx(wide, "Table1_by_trial.docx", landscape = TRUE, font_size = 9)

Each trial’s own table is kept in wide$trials, for example wide$trials[["Trial A"]].
